reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Slow, the Weaver (Book V); the frame (the wheel-bearer telling the gold-finder) is stated and omitted.

The barber's verses against consulting women and the wife's proverb against barbers and 'men of base condition' are cut; the lesson is to think any advice through yourself, not to ignore a wife; a discussion question now asks whether the villagers were right.

Fixed before approval: the yaksha's gender is consistent, a wrong pronoun in the wish is corrected, and the wife's plan is two cloths on two looms so it matches the two heads drawn side by side (disclosed).
Age band 12+: an innocent man is beaten to death by a mob, in two calm sentences, never drawn. No em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; one Codex gpt-5.6-sol generation with seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text.

Fixed before approval: the barber friend was drawn bald and pot-bellied, a comic stereotype tied to a caste-associated trade; one edit pass redrew him in panels 3 and 4 with an ordinary build and a full head of hair, and only those panels were composited back.
The two heads sit side by side, both grinning; four arms and two legs; comic, not frightening. Panel 6 shows villagers recoiling and pointing with empty hands; no beating or death is drawn.
No caste markers or modern objects; one alt text was corrected to match the picture.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; edited panels were re-checked by a separate agent.
